key_insight: Without input promises, approximate quantum circuit membership is PP-hard across multiple target-unitary sets and distance metrics, implying PP-hardness of related circuit optimization tasks.
engineering_relevance: The results establish worst-case barriers to minimizing total, non-Clifford, or superposition gate count and depth on hardware supporting Clifford+T.
method: Analyze promise-free membership near the identity, Clifford-only sets, and generalized-permutation-only sets.
Establish PP-hardness under trace-based, spectral, and operator metrics across wide approximation ranges.
Derive hardness consequences for circuit optimization, including selected cases using classical-reversible gates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical hardness results rather than empirical benchmarks, with PP-hardness for all non-trivial tolerances in specified trace-based cases.
watch_item: These are worst-case complexity results; they do not establish that practical heuristics or structured circuit instances are uniformly difficult.
paper_title: On the Hardness of Approximate Quantum Circuit Membership and Optimization
